round_question: The frozen contract (round 1-3) is a declarative surface + fingerprint + introspection + 19 behavioural probes, all executed on the *supplier* side. No upstream consumer was ever executed against the real IceDEM object: TensorPhysics' own tests/test_tensordem_adapter.py binds its adapter to a FakeIceDEM. Does the real consumer (tensorphysics.adapters.tensordem.TensorDEMAdapter + tensorphysics.Simulation) honour and observe the frozen clock / substep / load-stamp / no-restore semantics when it drives the real tensordem.IceDEM?
decision: Keep 'declarative contract + supplier-side probes' as the whole binding mechanism (A) versus add an executed consumer-side binding cross-check that runs the real TensorPhysics adapter against the real IceDEM and, on drift, classifies it (C).

alternatives.A: status quo: contract + introspection + supplier probes only; consumer side verified by FakeIceDEM unit tests in the other repo
alternatives.B: consumer side re-verified by a hand-written stub that copies the adapter logic into TensorDEM (no real cross-repo code path)
alternatives.C: execute the real TensorPhysics Simulation/TensorDEMAdapter against the real IceDEM, compare every observed number against the contract's declared value, and include controlled drift variants to prove the cross-check is not vacuous

hypothesis.H1: real consumer and real supplier agree with the contract on substep count, load_time stamping, load non-accumulation, clock advance and the no-restore claim; the executed numbers match the contract-declared values to machine precision
hypothesis.H0: the consumer re-sends accumulated loads (a naive accumulator), so the measured external impulse would be n(n+1)/2 dt F instead of n dt F

baseline_control: unmutated real IceDEM driven by the real adapter = control arm; three controlled drift variants (accumulating supplier, non-integer global dt, stale native clock) = treatment arms; FakeIceDEM unit test in TensorPhysics = pre-existing baseline for consumer coverage

thresholds_predeclared.load_time_stamp: max abs deviation <= 1e-12 s (structural: adapter uses the same k*dt formula as the reference)
thresholds_predeclared.external_impulse: rel error <= 1e-12 (structural identity, owner line 15% is 14 orders away)
thresholds_predeclared.adapt_reject_boundary: ratio+1e-10 accepted, ratio+1e-6 rejected, ratio 4.5 rejected (3/3)
thresholds_predeclared.drift_detection: 3/3 controlled variants classified, control arm clean

stopping_rule: single run; no threshold revised after seeing results. Any arm outside its predeclared tolerance is reported as FAIL (honest), not re-tuned.

environment.supplier: tensordem from this worktree src/ (frozen fingerprint pinned by FROZEN_FINGERPRINT test)
environment.consumer: /root/tensor-ecosystem/TensorPhysics/src (tensorphysics) resolved via TENSORPHYSICS_SRC or default sibling path; if absent the arm is reported WITHHELD, never faked
environment.hardware: 1 core, no GPU; whole run expected < 60 s
environment.seeds: no stochastic path in these arms (deterministic lattice, damping 0, drag 0)

confounders_and_controls: internal bond/contact forces are momentum-neutral by construction -> momentum claims use the model ledger (external_impulse_Ns) rather than net particle momentum
gravity is active -> impulse comparisons use the external load tensor actually handed in, not total force
float accumulation order differs between reference (k*dt) and adapter (context.time + i*dt) -> tolerance 1e-12 s predeclared, not exact bit equality
